Exports traces, metrics, and logs to a [NATS](https://nats.io/) server. Payloads
are published to NATS subjects using core NATS (fire-and-forget) or, optionally,
[JetStream](https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/jetstream) for durable,
acknowledged delivery.

> [!NOTE]
> This component is in development. The configuration surface described below is
> stable, but the publishing implementation is being contributed incrementally.

## Configuration

| Field       | Default            | Description |
| ----------- | ------------------ | ----------- |
| `endpoint`  | `nats://127.0.0.1:4222` | NATS server URL. |
| `pedantic`  | `true`             | Enable NATS [pedantic](https://docs.nats.io/reference/reference-protocols/nats-protocol#connect) mode. |
| `tls`       | (disabled)         | TLS client configuration. See [configtls](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/config/configtls/README.md). |
| `jetstream` | (unset)            | When set, publish via JetStream instead of core NATS. See [JetStream](#jetstream) below. |
| `logs`      |                    | Per-signal configuration for logs. See [Signal configuration](#signal-configuration). |
| `metrics`   |                    | Per-signal configuration for metrics. |
| `traces`    |                    | Per-signal configuration for traces. |

### Signal configuration

Each of `logs`, `metrics`, and `traces` accepts:

| Field                | Default                                        | Description |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `subject`            | `"otel_logs"` / `"otel_metrics"` / `"otel_spans"` | [OTTL value expression](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/pkg/ottl/README.md) evaluated to produce the [NATS subject](https://docs.nats.io/nats-concepts/subjects). String literals must be quoted. |
| `marshaler`          | `otlp_proto`                                   | Built-in payload marshaler: `otlp_proto` or `otlp_json`. Mutually exclusive with `encoding_extension`. |
| `encoding_extension` | (unset)                                        | Component ID of an [encoding extension](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/extension/encoding) to marshal payloads. Mutually exclusive with `marshaler`. |

### JetStream

When the `jetstream` block is present, every payload is published with JetStream
and the publish blocks until the server acknowledges persistence. A stream whose
subjects capture the configured signal subjects must already exist; this
exporter does not create or manage streams.

| Field             | Default | Description |
| ----------------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `domain`          | (server default) | JetStream domain, e.g. when publishing through a leaf node to a hub. |
| `publish_timeout` | `0` (no exporter deadline) | Maximum time to wait for each publish acknowledgement. |

### Authentication

At most one authentication method may be configured. See the NATS
[authentication docs](https://docs.nats.io/running-a-nats-service/configuration/securing_nats/auth_intro).

| Block            | Fields | Description |
| ---------------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `token`          | `token` | Token authentication. |
| `user`           | `username`, `password` | Username/password authentication. |
| `nkey`           | `public_key`, `seed` | NKey authentication. |
| `nkey_jwt`       | `jwt`, `seed` | NKey authentication via JWT. |
| `nkey_user_file` | `user_file` | NKey authentication via a credentials file. |

## Example

```yaml
exporters:
  # Minimal: core NATS, default subjects, OTLP protobuf.
  nats:
    endpoint: nats://localhost:4222

  # Full: JetStream durable publishing with auth, TLS, and per-signal subjects.
  nats/full:
    endpoint: nats://nats.example.com:4222
    tls:
      insecure: false
      ca_file: /etc/otel/certs/ca.crt
    user:
      username: otel
      password: ${env:NATS_PASSWORD}
    jetstream:
      domain: hub
      publish_timeout: 5s
    logs:
      subject: '"otel.logs." + resource.attributes["service.name"]'
      marshaler: otlp_proto
    metrics:
      subject: '"otel.metrics"'
      marshaler: otlp_json
    traces:
      subject: '"otel.spans"'

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [nats]
```
